W7211894364.title: Distilled Continuous Diffusion Language Models Can Write Code in Few Steps---or One
W7211894364.evidence: Abstract: pass@1 7.07 and pass@10 31.78/40.49 on HumanEval and MBPP+ vs. teacher and discrete-diffusion LMs; 0.7B model and denoising-step counts disclosed but no hardware or hyperparameters; training/inference code and checkpoints released (github.com/pengzhangzhi/plaidq).

W7213355055.title: KGMACG: Knowledge-Guided Multi-Agent Orchestration for Scalable Application-Level Code Generation
W7213355055.evidence: Abstract: three industrial case studies (E-Commerce, Campus Security, Stock Trading) against six named multi-agent baselines with DeepSeek R1 and gpt-5-codex-medium; no numeric results (only the >=95% coverage stopping rule), no hardware or hyperparameters, no artifact link.

W7213495287.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Cost-Efficient Large Language Models on Algorithmic Programming Tasks
W7213495287.evidence: Abstract: 992 problems under eight model/tool/prompt configurations, 7,936 executed requests, 12.9% correct; three models named and the Spring Boot/DTO protocol given, but problem source, hardware and generation hyperparameters are not; timing appears only as a stated limitation and no artifact is linked.

W7214056409.title: Quality over quantity: Diversity-aware data selection for efficient verilog code generation
W7214056409.evidence: Abstract (OpenAlex record has no abstract; read from official arXiv page 2609.22765): experiments on three LLMs and three benchmarks, Pass@1 +18.49-29.43% over full-dataset training and +1.36-7.95% over the best baseline; models and benchmarks are unnamed, hardware/hyperparameters absent, no artifact statement; the 80% training-time cut is training cost, not inference latency.

W7220428400.title: Improving the Energy-Efficiency of the Code Generated by LLMs through Effective Prompting
W7220428400.evidence: Abstract: 21 prompting strategies narrowed to 8, evaluated on 10 named LLMs in Python and C++ with energy cuts of up to 25%/17% relative to a baseline prompt; no correctness metric, dataset names, hardware or hyperparameters; execution-platform details absent; no artifact link.

W7215058388.title: Cracking Query Bottlenecks: Towards Efficiency-Oriented Text-to-SQL Generation
W7215058388.evidence: Abstract: EESQLBench pairs each question with expert-optimized SQL as an efficiency baseline; six named LLMs scored with CR and AR@k under correctness plus cost-based efficiency metrics; the benchmark is introduced but no release is stated, and hardware/generation settings are absent; efficiency is query execution cost, not model latency.

W4416784159.title: Don’t Use a Cannon to Kill a Fly: Lightweight Model Editing for LLMs to Correct Deprecated API Recommendations
W4416784159.evidence: Abstract: 10 editing techniques applied to three named LLMs on EDAPIBench (70+ APIs, 8 libraries, 3,000+ instances), with AdaLoRA-L vs AdaLoRA and correctness/specificity outcomes; benchmark composition is described but release is not stated, and hardware/editing hyperparameters are absent.

W7221747747.title: Diff Diffusion: Predicting Edit Paths with Diffusion Models for Efficient Code Editing
W7221747747.evidence: Abstract: public edit-completion benchmarks, edit-prediction evaluations and online validation, matching or leading autoregressive baselines with 2.78x faster inference and 39.0% P50 latency cut; accuracy is stated only qualitatively, benchmarks and hardware are unnamed, and no artifact is linked.

W7222234395.title: HERO: Harnessing Evidence for Test-time Refinement and Prompt Optimization in Program Generation
W7222234395.evidence: Abstract: four SQL, Cypher and Python benchmarks, pass@1 +7.6 over the initial-prompt baseline and +2.0 from test-time refinement, plus execution-efficiency gains; benchmarks, LLMs, hardware and hyperparameters are all unnamed; no artifact link.

W7221835407.title: Smells Like Prompt Spirit: Evaluating Energy Efficiency and Performance of Local LLM Inference on CPU vs GPU
W7221835407.evidence: Abstract: five local LLMs on HumanEval-X and MBPP+, 0-shot vs 3-shot, CPU vs a dedicated GPU cluster, with 99.8% runtime and up to 89.4% energy reductions and functional-correctness measurements; model names and GPU model absent, prompting variants given but no serving stack; no artifact link.

W7223112641.title: Self-Decomposing Diffusion for Code Generation
W7223112641.evidence: Abstract: five benchmarks and two 7B diffusion backbones, pass@1 up to +31.1 points and 7.5-13.7x faster decoding vs the base models, +23.5 points over a fine-tuning baseline with lower latency; backbone names, benchmark names and hardware are absent; no artifact link.
